get.description: Merges multiple crashes so they will be treated as the same crash in reports.

parameters.name: idSite
parameters.description: The site ID.

parameters.name: idLogCrashes
parameters.description: Crash IDs to merge, either as an array or a comma-separated list. Example: [12, 34] or 12 or "12,34".

get.description: Unmerge a previously merged crash group.

parameters.name: idSite
parameters.description: The site ID.

parameters.name: idLogCrash
parameters.description: The crash group ID to unmerge.

get.description: Gets every merged crash group for a site.

parameters.name: idSite
parameters.description: The site ID.

200.description: Crash groups keyed by group ID.

get.description: Gets the list of unique crash types that were tracked for a specific site.

parameters.name: idSite
parameters.description: The site ID.

parameters.name: filter_limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of types to return, or false to return all.

get.description: Set whether a crash should be ignored when tracking or whether it should no longer be ignored.

parameters.name: idSite
parameters.description: The site ID.

parameters.name: idLogCrash
parameters.description: The crash ID.

parameters.name: ignore
parameters.description: If true or non-zero, the crash will be ignored. Ignored crashes are not logged when encountered during tracking. If false or 0, the crash will be unignored.

get.description: Get the list of currently ignored crashes for a site.

parameters.name: idSite
parameters.description: The site ID.

200.description: The list of ignored crashes. Each entry contains information about the specific crash, including the crash message, originating source and other information.

get.description: Gets information for a specific crash including it's message, originating source and other information, if one can be found. The most recently tracked crash and page URL that encountered the crash will also be included.

parameters.name: idSite
parameters.description: The site ID.

parameters.name: idLogCrash
parameters.description: The crash ID.

200.description: Crash summary details, including the latest crash event info when available.

get.description: Gets the crash visit context, which includes information about the most recent visits that encountered the crash and the actions that occurred just before the crash.

parameters.name: idLogCrash
parameters.description: The crash ID.

parameters.name: idSite
parameters.description: The site ID.

parameters.name: period
parameters.description: The period string (eg, day, week, month).

parameters.name: date
parameters.description: The date string for the period.

parameters.name: segment
parameters.description: Optional segment definition, or false for none.

parameters.name: filter_limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of crashes to return.

parameters.name: filter_offset
parameters.description: Offset for paging.

parameters.name: fetchRecentActions
parameters.description: Whether to fetch the most recent actions or not. By default they are fetched, but you may want to skip this for performance reasons.

get.description: Gets the list of every crash tracked for a site.

parameters.name: idSite
parameters.description: The site ID.

parameters.name: filter_sort_column
parameters.description: The crash property to sort by.

parameters.name: filter_sort_order
parameters.description: 'asc' or 'desc'.

parameters.name: filter_limit
parameters.description: The max number of crashes to return (cannot be greater than 10000).

parameters.name: filter_offset
parameters.description: The offset for paging.

tags.name: CrashAnalytics
tags.description:
The Crash Analytics API lets you 1) ignore/unignore crashes tracked by Matomo 2) request information about individual crashes and 3) request all your Crash Analytics reports and metrics. 1) You can ignore crashes so they will no longer be tracked, or unignore previously ignored crashes so they will reappear again in your reports.

2) You can merge different crashes together so they will be treated as a single crash in reports, or unmerge previously merged groups. You can also get the list of all merged crash groups for a site.

3) You can request summarized information about a single crash as well as query the entire list of raw tracked crash information:
- get a list of all the different crash types that were tracked via CrashAnalytics.getCrashTypes
- get the list of currently ignored crashes via CrashAnalytics.getIgnoredCrashes
- get summarized information about a single crash via CrashAnalytics.getCrashSummary
- get information about the actions that preceeded a crash via CrashAnalytics.getCrashVisitContext
- query every crash that has been tracked for a site via CrashAnalytics.getAllCrashes

4) Request all metrics and reports about crashes that occur on your website:
- How often different crash messages appear and which source file originated them
- Which crashes have disappeared and not been seen in the last several days
- Which crashes have recently reappeared after an absence
- Which crashes are new and have never been seen before
- Which pages have the most crashes and what those crashes are
- Which source files generate the most crashes and what those crashes are
- Which crash categories appear the most and what crashes appear for those categories
- Which crashes originate from first party source files (in other words, source files hosted by your website)
- Which crashes originate from third party source files (in other words, source files from third party websites, generally outside your control)
- What crashes are currently occurring on your website, within the last N minutes
- Which of the crashes that are currently occurring are new
- Which of the crashes that are currently occurring were absent but have reappeared
- What crashes have just been absent long enough to be considered "disappeared"

And the following metrics:
- How many times a crash occurs
- How often a visit encounters at least one crash
- How many unique crashes were tracked
- How many new crashes were tracked
- How many crashes that were tracked were absent for some time, but have since reappeared
- How often a page view encounters at least one crash
- How many crashes are currently ignored
